reasoning: Both findings of the first round are closed in design.md D2, its Risks list and tasks 1.1-1.3; every class now rests on an observation or a named test.

simpler.evidence: design.md carries three rejected alternatives: D1 (keep the rows before the writes -- a fresh install, the reproduction's own case, would read no Project and print every workflow), D2 (`claude plugin marketplace list --json` / `claude plugin list --json`, the readers skill_check.py uses -- rejected on the observation that the first prints no `autoUpdate`, so a file read remains, plus the spec scenario 'no command it issued is a `claude` command' and a real CLI inside the test Runner), D4 (`unchanged` rows instead of omission). A smaller row set is not a live option: #269's brief fixes the six rows, and `project-visibility` + `project-areas` + `project-workflows` come from one request, the template's `Area` options as a second aliased field rather than a new constant. No new abstraction: the reads live in `_manual`/`_run` and reuse the existing `gh` boundary.

map.evidence: Nine delta scenarios, nine map entries: Observed done -> test_observed_manual_rows_are_omitted; Unreadable state -> test_unreadable_manual_state_is_printed; Manual actions -> test_manual_actions_are_printed; Review prerequisites -> test_review_prerequisites_are_printed; Channel render -> test_plugin.py::test_marketplace_follows_stable; Machine channel step -> test_manual_actions_are_printed; Consumer render -> test_init_config.py::test_pre_commit_block_references_the_hook; Consumer file without the block -> test_init_conflicts.py::test_conflict_fails_closed[pre-commit-without-block]; Per-clone row -> test_manual_actions_are_printed. Each named test exists or is written in task 1.2, and the three tests carrying new assertions are parametrized over both modes; `test_unreadable_manual_state_is_printed` now covers three read families (secret 403, malformed plugin file, failing project read).

red.evidence: tasks 1.1-1.3: the harness change first, with `python -m pytest tests/publisher -q` green before any new assertion; then the three test functions of the map; then `check_red` on seven node ids whose ids match the parametrizations (`[--dry-run]`, `[--confirm]`, `[secret-403]`, `[plugin-malformed]`, `[project-read]`), committed as `test(distribution): manual rows follow observed state`. Each fails in its body against today's `_manual`: the fixed strings carry no `(cannot read: `, the workflows row names all five workflows, the rows are printed before `_perform`'s lines rather than last, and every row prints on an already-done state. No `no RED` task is needed; the three pre-existing map entries and test_review_prerequisites_are_printed assert clauses of the modified requirements the plan does not change.

platform.evidence: proposal.md -- Why dates every read (2026-09-30, gh 2.87.3, Windows 11): `gh secret list --json name` output and the 403 stderr of an unpermitted repository; `projectV2` `public`, `workflows{name enabled}` and `field(name:"Area"){options{name}}` read on both the copy (#9, seven enabled workflows named) and the template (#4, eight), with `gh project copy` leaving `Auto-add to project` absent rather than disabled; `known_marketplaces.json` and `installed_plugins.json` entries including `autoUpdate` and `scope: user`, and `claude plugin marketplace list --json` printing no `autoUpdate`; pre-commit 4.6.0's `# ID: 138fd403232d2ddd5efb44317e38bf03` and `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-push`. `repositoryOwner{... on ProjectV2Owner}` is observed on a user owner and already carries PROJECTS_QUERY in production. The completeness of the secret list, previously asserted, is now the observation in D2's `review-secret` bullet (`GH_DEBUG=api` shows gh 2.87.3 requesting `.../actions/secrets?per_page=100`; `gh secret list --help` has no limit flag), with the residue in Risks: beyond 100 secrets the token may be missed, a false outstanding row and never a false omission. `ProjectV2Workflow` exposing only `name`, `enabled` and ids is recorded as the reason the target statuses stay out of scope (Non-Goals).

replaced.evidence: No project-declared input is replaced and no guard dropped. The rows keep their text and targets; `WORKFLOWS` stays the target text and the required set stays the `state` spec's five built-in workflows (D3). The tests' `_gh_kind` guard gains `secret list` as a `read` (task 1.1), which keeps 'no command it issued writes a secret' provable and still fails the test on any other `gh` command. The user-profile requirement ('The running installer SHALL write nothing in the user profile', with its byte-identical scenario) still holds: the two plugin files are read under `ctx.home` and never created (D2, D5), and the existing footprint tests remain the catcher for that. Where `_gh_json`'s `check=True` guard does not fit the new position of the reads, D2 replaces it deliberately with `ctx.call(..., check=False)` plus guarded parsing and names what that costs (a failed read becomes three `(cannot read: …)` rows instead of an error) -- D1 and task 2.1 still say 'a fresh `_repository` read', which D2 defines as the guarded `gh repo view`.

catcher.evidence: design Risks names the session-start check for a changed plugin-file shape: `.claude/agent-process-check.py` (templates/skill_check.py) runs in the consumer's `SessionStart` hook group that `init` writes, and returns `agent-process skill not loaded (not installed at user scope: claude plugin install ...)`, reaching the person at every session start; it reads `claude plugin list --json`, so it is independent of the raw files `init` reads -- traced. The pre-push clone risk is caught by SKILL.md Install step 4's 'in each clone', which the plan keeps. The marketplace half (`ref: stable`, `autoUpdate`) and the >100-secret case have no second catcher; there the printed row is the carrier -- `(cannot read: …)` for a changed file shape, the outstanding row itself for a truncated secret list (principle IV), and the design says so.

length.evidence: ADDED requirement, sentence 1 (34 words): 'classified after the run's writes' is asserted by test_manual_actions_are_printed[--confirm] (the workflows row can name only `Auto-add to project` if the copy `_perform` just made is read); 'end their output with the manual rows' is now asserted in both modes by task 1.2's order assertion (no non-`manual` line follows the first `manual` line); 'omit a row whose target state is observed' by test_observed_manual_rows_are_omitted. Sentence 2 (25 words): `(cannot read: <reason>)` and exit 0 are asserted for three read families -- `[secret-403]`, `[plugin-malformed]` and `[project-read]` on `--confirm`, the case that would otherwise turn a finished install into exit 1; the `pre-push` read has no failing path to assert (an unset `core.hooksPath` exits 1 by design and an unreadable hook file leaves the row outstanding). Modified requirements: the workflow-naming clause, the `Area`-equality clause and the private-Project clause are asserted by test_manual_actions_are_printed or test_observed_manual_rows_are_omitted; the `pre-push` and `plugin-channel` conditions by the kept assertions plus the omission test. SKILL.md Install steps 3-4 (task 2.3) only shorten prose and keep the `quality-command` word the existing test asserts.

bespoke.evidence: The plan adds no script, hook or gate: four reads inside `_run`/`_manual` of the existing installer, and no new dependency (proposal -- Impact). The standard readers for the plugin state (`claude plugin marketplace list --json` / `claude plugin list --json`, used by skill_check.py) are weighed in D2 and rejected on an observation, and the Project read stays on the existing `gh` boundary and `PROJECTS_QUERY` pattern rather than a new client. The problem each read closes is the table of #269.
